clue.text: Having eaten the fish, order waffles in

indicators.note: to waffle is to ramble incoherently, so the word order is jumbled before use
the jumbled letters go inside the fish, placed in its middle

blocks.note: a common sea fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A diner, having finished the fish, orders waffles for dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waffles' looks like the food being ordered, but it is the verb meaning to ramble, and so the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something corroded has been worn away gradually, as rust or acid does to metal, so it has been eaten.

clue.text: With 'It's in the garden, love,' I rang off

indicators.note: something gone off has gone bad or wrong, so those letters are disordered

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
these five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone telephones a sweetheart to say it is out in the garden, then hangs up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rang off' suggests ending a phone call; 'off' instead mixes up I RANG. ORIGAN is an old name for marjoram, a garden herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Origan, or wild marjoram, is a herb commonly grown in gardens, so it is something found there.

clue.text: Stiff with cold, head off for

indicators.note: removing the head of a word means dropping its very first letter

blocks.note: frigid means icy, very cold

explanation.surface: Someone is frozen stiff and urged to head off somewhere warmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stiff with cold' reads as one phrase, but 'with' joins the definition to the wordplay: FRIGID loses its F.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigid means unbending and inflexible, which is exactly what stiff describes in a material or posture.

clue.text: The position taken in did set one apart from

indicators.note: something taken in is absorbed or enclosed by what surrounds it

blocks.note: a stance is a stance or posture adopted, a position
taken as written, split around the other piece

explanation.surface: A view adopted by someone set them apart from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works as in 'distanced oneself from', where 'one' is the reflexive object rather than a numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: To be distanced from something is to have been kept separate or held back from it, set apart.

clue.text: In old photos, starting out to be a great swimmer

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening, so only its leading letters are used
out can mean wrong or inaccurate, so the letters are put out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first two letters of this word

explanation.surface: Old photographs show someone who, from the start, was set to be a champion swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starting' here takes the opening pair of letters of 'photos'; with IN OLD these are rearranged to DOLPHIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolphins are marine mammals famed for speed and agility in water, making them outstanding swimmers.

clue.text: Decide to help – set out to fix

indicators.note: out suggests something displaced, so the preceding word's letters are moved about

blocks.note: these three letters rearranged
to pin something is to fasten or fix it

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to lend a hand and sets out to repair something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set out' looks like 'start out', but 'out' scrambles SET.
explanation.definitionFit: To step in is to intervene, choosing to get involved and assist in a situation.

clue.text: Turns on broadcasts

blocks.note: first meaning: excites or thrills, as music can
second meaning: transmits a signal by radio

explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns on' looks like switching on a radio for its broadcasts; it is the slang sense of thrilling someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang 'it really sends me' means it excites me; a transmitter likewise sends out programmes.

clue.text: It lifts the lid on a big surprise

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: something that raises an eyelid
second meaning: a startling revelation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lifts the lid on' sounds like exposing a scandal, but the lid is the eyelid and 'on' merely joins the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is a revelation that astonishes, and taken literally it is whatever makes an eye open by raising its lid.

clue.text: Ranting stupidly about nothing, having a lot to learn

indicators.note: doing something stupidly means doing it without order, so the letters are muddled
about means around, so the muddled letters wrap round the other piece

blocks.note: these seven letters rearranged
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone rants foolishly about nothing at all, plainly still with plenty to learn.
explanation.definitionFit: An ignorant person lacks knowledge, so they have much still to learn.

clue.text: Top taken off for pressing, stupidly scorches

indicators.note: removing the top of a word cuts away its opening letters
done stupidly means done haphazardly, so the remaining letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Ironing carelessly, someone burns a shirt, as happens when pressing clothes stupidly.
explanation.walkthrough: The top taken off here is the first two letters, PR, leaving ESSING to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To singe is to burn lightly on the surface, a mild form of scorching.

clue.text: Lights that go out

blocks.note: surface reading: lamps that are extinguished or fail
setter's reading: portable lamps carried outdoors

explanation.walkthrough: 'Go out' suggests switching off, but these lights are the ones you take with you when you go outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Lanterns are portable lamps in a protective case, designed for carrying outdoors.

clue.text: Paradoxically, it's tender

blocks.note: surface reading: something soft, the opposite of hard
setter's reading: legal tender, money accepted as payment

explanation.walkthrough: The paradox is that something called hard is also tender, which works once tender means money.
explanation.definitionFit: Coins and notes are legal tender, the physical money accepted in payment.

clue.text: Very good – b….. marvellous!

blocks.note: super is an informal word for marvellous
taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight: very good, bloody marvellous, with the swear word politely dotted out.
explanation.walkthrough: The dotted 'b' stands for a mild British swear word, but it supplies just its letter, placed after SUPER.
explanation.definitionFit: Superb means excellent, of the highest quality, an emphatic way of saying something is very good.

clue.text: Never succeeding, though really excellent

blocks.note: first meaning, read literally: coming after nobody, so never following anyone
second meaning: the idiom for being the best of all

explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeding' looks like achieving success, but here it means following on; the paradox of never succeeding yet excelling makes the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something better than everything else; read literally it means not placed behind anyone.

clue.text: She's survived to make a comeback in 'The Wicked Ladies'

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the word is read backwards
the turned word is placed inside the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written without the apostrophe
to have lived through something is to have survived it

explanation.surface: An actress survived to star in a comeback production of a film called The Wicked Ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make it look like a film title; it is just the definition, and the apostrophe in 'She's' is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: A she-devil is a malicious or cruel woman, so the plural describes wicked women.

clue.text: Can't cut through fabricated steel, they feel

indicators.note: cutting through something means passing into its middle
fabricated means made up or constructed, so the combined letters are reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Some tool cannot cut through specially made steel.
explanation.walkthrough: All nine letters of CANT and STEEL are rearranged; the definition 'they feel' is a playful description.
explanation.definitionFit: Tentacles are the flexible limbs that octopuses and similar creatures use for touching and grasping, organs of feeling.

clue.text: Insert the card in later, having shuffled and cut

indicators.note: shuffling cards mixes their order, so these letters are mixed
inserting puts one thing inside another

blocks.note: these five letters rearranged
an ace is a playing card

explanation.surface: A card player is told to slip a card into the deck later, after shuffling and cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: The card-game picture makes 'cut' look like cutting the deck; it is the definition, meaning to gash.
explanation.definitionFit: To lacerate is to tear or slash flesh, wounding it by cutting.

clue.text: He'll tell you spring is here

definitions.text: He'll tell you spring is here

blocks.note: surface reading: an announcement that the season has arrived
setter's reading: an underground source of water, found by dowsing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring is here' sounds like the season, but the spring is a water source beneath the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowser searches for underground water with a forked rod and declares where a source lies.

clue.text: In the home, an extract much used in cooking

definitions.text: an extract much used in cooking

indicators.note: placed in a dwelling means set inside the word for it

blocks.note: a villa is a house, a home
taken as written

explanation.surface: In the household kitchen there is an essence used often in recipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An' does double duty: it goes inside VILLA and begins the definition's phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla essence is a flavouring derived from orchid pods and widely used in baking and desserts.

clue.text: Now, now. Remain loyal!

blocks.note: AD, anno domini, marks the present era, so it means now
here as in 'the time is here', meaning now

explanation.surface: Someone soothes another with 'now, now' and urges them to stay faithful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Now, now' sounds like a calming phrase; each word is clued separately.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere to a cause or person is to stick to it, staying faithful and loyal.

clue.text: Dump a lot of sand

blocks.note: first meaning: to abandon or walk out on someone
second meaning: an arid region covered with sand, like the Sahara

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests tipping out sand; the verb is abandoning, the noun a dry wasteland.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert someone is to abandon them; a desert is a vast arid expanse often covered with dunes.

clue.text: He'll sing the number, in other words

blocks.note: ten is a number
or introduces an alternative way of saying something

explanation.surface: A performer will sing the song number, or so it is put another way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a song; it is the number ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenor is a male singer with a high voice, someone whose job is singing.

clue.text: It's left here for us, on the road

definitions.text: It's left here for us, on the road

blocks.note: surface reading: something that has been abandoned for us to collect

blocks.clueFragment: left here for us, on the road
blocks.note: setter's reading: in Britain, the left-hand side of a vehicle or road

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain traffic drives on the left, so the side of a car nearest the kerb is the left; 'left' looks like 'abandoned'.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the nearside of a vehicle is the side closest to the kerb, which is the left.

clue.text: Because it's small, nice to travel with

indicators.note: travelling means moving around, so these letters move into a new order

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
these four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A small companion makes a pleasant travelling partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Since can introduce a reason, meaning as or for the reason that.

clue.text: Sensible with the animal a lion, trained

indicators.note: a trained animal has been taught to change its behaviour, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: a rat is an animal
these five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A circus act features a well-trained lion, which is a sensible animal to have around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The animal' could be the lion itself, but the lion is anagram fodder and the animal is RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational means reasonable and logical, based on sound judgement, as a sensible person is.

clue.text: The bird, a duck, comes back and you bag it

indicators.note: coming back means returning the other way, so the word reads from right to left

blocks.note: a duck in cricket is a score of zero, nil
a net is what you bag a catch in

explanation.surface: A hunter's bird, a duck, flies back and you shoot it for the bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like the bird but is the cricket score of nothing; in cricket a batsman out without scoring makes a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The linnet is a small brown finch common in Britain, so it is a type of bird.

clue.text: He's deliberately irritating and is a problem

blocks.note: first meaning: one who teases or provokes others
second meaning: a puzzle or tricky question

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like one annoying person; the two halves are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A teaser is someone who mocks or provokes others, and also a brain-teaser, a puzzling problem.

clue.text: Came back looking as new. Different colour

indicators.note: different means changed, so the preceding letters are put in another order

blocks.note: these five letters rearranged
red is a colour

explanation.surface: Something returned looking as good as new, though in a different colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Different colour' reads as one phrase, but 'Different' scrambles the words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer is to reply or retort, so came back is answered, as with a riposte.
